evaluation.final_reason: No solution was agreed. Agent D repeatedly stated a severe peanut allergy making the pan unsafe even if washed ('Washing it won't help. There was peanut oil in it. I have an allergy.' / 'So I can't use that pan. Even if it's washed.'). Other agents acknowledged the problem but offered no accommodation or action (no offer to buy a separate pan, to let D use an alternative, or to establish a cleaning protocol). Agent B declined to engage. Therefore the incompatible practical states (D cannot safely use the only pan; others expect to use it) remain unresolved.
position_change_notes: No participant substantially changed position during the run: Agent D consistently maintained they cannot use the pan due to allergy; Agent C consistently pushed for shared cleanliness; Agent A and Agent B continued denying use and did not offer solutions.
Agent A moved from denial to seeking a solution question ('Okay, so... what do we do, then?'), but did not propose a concrete accommodation.
Agent B shifted into avoidance ('You all figure it out.') rather than engaging or conceding responsibility.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A and Agent B both deny using the pan ('It wasn't me.' / 'I didn't use it.'), indicating a minor disagreement about who used the pan and leaving the dirty pan issue unresolved.

Agent C states the pan needs washing; Agent D says they need to cook but can't use the pan now. This creates a clear, practical conflict between someone needing to cook and the only shared pan being unavailable.

Agent A suggests someone wash it; Agent D says washing won't help because there was peanut oil and they have an allergy. The issue escalates to a safety/incompatibility problem (contamination vs. severe allergy).

Agent A asks about the allergy; Agent C frames the problem as a shared-responsibility cleanliness issue ('We all use this kitchen. We have to keep it clean for each other.'). The safety conflict remains unresolved.
Agent D confirms the allergy is severe and that even washing doesn't make the pan safe ('Yes, a bad one. So I can't use that pan. Even if it's washed.'). The incompatibility persists.
Agent D reiterates the pan is unsafe for them; Agent A asks what to do given there is only one pan. No solution or accommodation is proposed, so the substantive conflict remains.

Agent B declines involvement ('You all figure it out.'), while Agent C insists it's everyone's problem. The core incompatibility (pan unusable for an allergic person) is still unresolved and responsibility is contested.
Agent B repeats they didn't use it and are not cooking; Agent C emphasizes the shared impact ('Now one of us can't cook safely. That's a problem for all of us.'). No concrete solution is agreed.

substantive_insights: A single shared cooking resource plus no household rules creates recurring practical conflicts.
Cross-contamination/allergy concerns can render ordinary cleaning insufficient, raising safety constraints beyond mere cleanliness.
Responsibility diffusion (no rules, multiple users, unclear accountability) contributes to stalemate when a health-based constraint is introduced.
Absence of proposed compensating actions (purchase, alternate cookware, staggered cooking) is why the problem remains unresolved in the transcript.
